title: "PSC / ownership (status)"
---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Status: In progress.** Reconnaissance of the PSC bulk snapshot is complete; the extractor is
in design. No PSC dataset is published, and — by decision — only **code** will be, never the
data. This page describes what the recon found and the design that follows from it.
:::

## Summary

"PSC" means *persons with significant control* — broadly, the people and entities that own or
control a UK company. Companies House publishes a daily bulk snapshot of this register, and this
project has analysed it end to end to decide what can responsibly be built from it. The short
version: the snapshot is large (about 16 million records), it retains history back to 2016, and
it is rich enough to support company-level ownership features — but it is personal data, it has
no stable identifier for a person, and its internal structure is full of traps. So the plan is to
publish **code and company-level aggregates only**, keep any person-level table private, and
state match confidence honestly rather than imply a clean ownership graph.

This is deliberately a **status page**, not a dataset. It records the measured findings and the
design decisions; it does not publish results.

## Details

### What the recon found

The recon ran over **all 32 parts of the 2026-09-18 snapshot — 15,952,486 records, 0 bad lines**,
in 404 seconds, joined against the 2026-08-01 Basic Company Data (5,695,465 live companies). Every
figure below traces to `docs/recon-psc-results.md` / `docs/recon-psc-results.json`; the full
write-up is `docs/recon-psc.md`. **[Checked]** (project measurement).

- **History is reconstructable from 2016-04-06.** Ceased PSC records are retained — 2,655,316
  records (16.6%) carry a `ceased_on` date, and every notified-on year since 2016 keeps a ceased
  cohort. The product spans **10,917,257 distinct companies — nearly double the live register** —
  so it holds PSC history for companies no longer live. 62,986 companies appear only as ceased
  records. Point-in-time control reconstruction is therefore feasible.
- **Statements exist, segregated at the tail.** 922,564 records (5.8%) are
  `persons-with-significant-control-statement` records (e.g. "no PSC identified"), all in parts
  31–32. The one-part probe that preceded the full recon wrongly concluded there were none —
  because parts 1–30 genuinely contain none.
- **Partitioning is meaningless.** The ~32 parts are neither random samples nor company-number
  ranges — every part spans essentially the whole register, statements are segregated into
  31–32, and recent years cluster in parts 25–30. **No per-part rate is usable; stream all
  parts.**
- **Composition.** Individual PSCs 87.1%, corporate 6.7%, statements 5.8%, legal-person 0.1%,
  overseas-entity beneficial-owner variants ~0.3%, plus 545 super-secure records and 108
  exemptions.
- **Individuals.** Date of birth (year and month) present on 100%; identity-verification details
  on 50.6% (ECCTA rollout, start years 2025–2026); `is_sanctioned` present on 34,444, true on 17.
- **Corporate PSCs.** A registration number is present on 91.0%, of which 77.9% resolve to a live
  company — a usable company-to-company ownership edge.
- **Natures of control.** 35,169,887 assertions over 15,029,053 records; 55 distinct base rights
  once suffix families (`-as-firm`, `-as-trust`, `-limited-liability-partnership`,
  `-registered-overseas-entity`) are stripped.

### Data-quality traps (document them before using)

- **No stable person ID.** Linking the same person across companies is a fuzzy join. On a
  conservative key — (forename, surname, birth year, birth month) — **28.8%** of keys appear on
  ≥2 records and **28.0%** on ≥2 distinct companies: cross-company linkage is common, but the
  method's confidence must be stated, not assumed. See [person matching in
  pitfalls](../guide/pitfalls.qmd).
- **Dirty dates.** 14,554 records have `ceased_on` before `notified_on`; 23,916 `notified_on`
  dates predate the 2016 regime (min `1083-01-01`); **272** `ceased_on` dates fall outside
  2016–2026 (269 before 2016; 3 after: `2924`, `9998`, `9999`). 17,729 individuals imply an age
  under 16 at notification, 55 over 110. A cleaning rule is required before any time-series use.
  Source: `docs/recon-psc-results.json` (`overall.ceased_on.years`), corroborated by the loader's
  `f_ceased_out_of_range` (see `docs/AUDIT.md`, "PSC loader Stage-1"). An earlier draft said 97,
  which was the 2016 ceased-date count (97,485) mis-transcribed. **[Checked]**
- **One-shot snapshot.** Only today's file is served; corrections over time are lost unless you
  archive snapshots yourself.

### Design decisions that follow

- **Code only, never the data.** PSC records are personal data, and users can download the
  snapshot directly from Companies House, so there is nothing to gain and real risk in
  republishing it. The repository will ship the extractor and methodology only. Source:
  `docs/recon-psc.md`, deck slide 17 notes.
- **Private person table, public per-company aggregates.** Any person-level linkage table stays
  private. What could be published (as code producing them, not as a shipped dataset) are
  **company-level** features: PSC counts, corporate ownership chains, how many companies a person
  controls (with honest match confidence), and unresolved-ownership statement flags — none of
  which name an individual.
- **Nationality excluded.** Nationality is present on 100% of individual records (4,666 distinct
  raw values) but is **measured for data-quality documentation only and excluded from any
  product** — a deliberate scope decision. Source: `docs/recon-psc.md`.
- **Honest match confidence.** Because there is no stable person ID, any companies-per-person
  statistic is reported with its matching method and confidence, never as a settled fact.

### Prior work to build on

This is well-trodden ground, and the plan is to reuse and benchmark against existing work rather
than reinvent it (full summaries on [the prior-work page](../evidence/prior-work.qmd)):

- **Global Witness + DataKind UK**, "The Companies We Keep" (2018) — matched people on name +
  birth month/year + address; the natural benchmark for this project's person matching.
- **Open Ownership** — its `bods-uk-psc-pipeline` publishes UK ownership in the Beneficial
  Ownership Data Standard, and has been combined with procurement and sanctions data.
- **OpenSanctions** — its `gb-coh-psc` converter turns Companies House ownership data into a
  standard graph format.
